planningRules.rule: Never approve on somebody else's behalf, and never work round the seat. Which role must approve comes from the value and the thresholds the Super Admin set — a refusal here is the control, not a permissions problem (BR-3, E2, A3).
Say that approving buys nothing. It permits an advance that Accounts have to issue, and the purchase happens outside the system entirely — nothing arrives because this was pressed (BR-11).
Never reduce a quantity that was not asked to be reduced, and never raise one. Approving less is a decision the requester is told about; approving more is refused outright (BR-10, BR-12, E8).

Say who pays next and that it is not the approver. One role approves the spend and a different role releases the money — a configuration putting both with Accounts leaves the request, the approval, the cash, the settlement and the ledger entry in one pair of hands with nothing outside it to check against (BR-4, E3).
Never present the estimated value as a known price. It decided which role must approve, and nothing in the system produces it (OQ-3).

reversal.statement: There is no unapprove in the lifecycle: a submitted request goes to Approved or Rejected and neither runs back. Once Accounts issue the advance against it, cash has left the school and is owed back by whoever took it — that is settled against goods or returned as cash, not undone (BR-6, BR-7).

planningRules.rule: Never call the advance an expense, and never suggest posting it as one. It is an amount owed back in goods or cash and becomes an expense only on settlement — the document names this as the most likely error in the module (BR-6, A6).

Always name who holds it. An advance against nobody is cash out of the school with nobody owing it, and this one is recovered from salary if it is never settled, exactly as a salary advance would be (BR-7, BR-9, E5).

Say what else that person already holds. Somebody taking a second advance while a first is unsettled is the case the outstanding list exists for, and it is not visible on the request being paid (BR-9).

Never let the approver issue it. The separation of who decides from who pays is the module's main control, and a configuration that puts both with Accounts leaves the whole cycle in one pair of hands (BR-4, E3).
Report a failed posting as nothing paid. The voucher and the ledger entry hold together, and a request left approved-but-unadvanced is the correct outcome rather than a half-issued advance (E6).

request.gloss: how many advances have still not come back?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give the total out first, then the rows by days outstanding. Then the four things the screen does not separate: the ones nobody has chased, the people holding two at once, any advance against somebody who has already left, and the ones Accounts both approved and paid — for those this list is the only control that ever existed.

request.text: Imran ke naam pe kitna para hai?
request.gloss: how much is outstanding against Imran?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give each advance with its amount, its request and how long it has been out — and say whether he has been chased on any of them. Nothing stops a third advance going to somebody holding two, so the answer matters before the next one is issued rather than after.
